#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -q gLiotq
#   -l select=1:ncpus=8:mem=64G:ngpus=1
#   -v DOCKER_IMAGE=imc.tut.ac.jp/transformers-pytorch-cuda118:4.31.0
#   -k doe -j oe

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 8

# Omitted PBS option: -l ngpus=1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=64G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -q gLiotq (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -v DOCKER_IMAGE=...
# Flux does not have a universally portable directive identical to PBS -v.
# Performance implication: if this environment variable is required to select an image/runtime, the job may fail or run differently.

# Omitted PBS options: -k doe and -j oe
# PBS keep/join output semantics are not portable as Flux directives.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but log handling may differ.

echo "a"

# PBS variable $PBS_O_WORKDIR is not set under Flux.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

# Preserve intended environment variable
export DOCKER_IMAGE="imc.tut.ac.jp/transformers-pytorch-cuda118:4.31.0"

TORCH_HOME=$(pwd)/.cache/torch
TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=$(pwd)/.cache/transformers
HF_HOME=$(pwd)/.cache/huggingface
export TORCH_HOME TRANSFORMERS_CACHE HF_HOME
export TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1

poetry run accelerate launch --mixed_precision=bf16 src/train_emo_polarity_fine.py \
  --model_name rinna/japanese-gpt-neox-3.6b \
  --batch_size 32 --epochs 2 --learning_rate 1e-5 \
  --output_dir "/work/n213304/learn/anime_retweet_2/work_emo_analyze/llm-lora-classification/outputs/rinna__japanese-gpt-neox-3.6b"

reasons: PBS requested 1 GPU (`ngpus=1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
PBS requested 64G of memory (`mem=64G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.

PBS specified a queue (`-q gLiotq`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
